components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Journey of Earth's continuous water movement through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.title: Overview
components.description: Water on Earth is constantly moving and changing states. The total amount of water remains largely constant, recycling through the atmosphere, land, and oceans.

components.title: Evaporation and Transpiration
components.body: Solar energy heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, causing it to change from a liquid to a gas called water vapor. Plants also release water vapor from their leaves through a process called transpiration.
components.takeaway: Heat from the sun powers the upward movement of water into the atmosphere.

components.title: Condensation
components.body: As water vapor rises into the cooler upper atmosphere, it cools down and changes back into tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals. These droplets cluster around microscopic particles in the air to form clouds and fog.
components.takeaway: Cooling temperatures aloft cause water vapor to condense into visible clouds.

components.title: Precipitation and Collection
components.body: When condensed water droplets in clouds grow too heavy to stay suspended by upward air currents, they fall back to Earth as precipitation (rain, snow, sleet, or hail). This water collects in oceans, rivers, and aquifers, or forms runoff over land.
components.takeaway: Gravity brings water back to the surface, completing the cycle and feeding Earth's water bodies.

components.title: Worked Example: Morning Dew and Puddles
components.body: Consider a puddle after a rainstorm. Over a few hours, the water seems to disappear—this is evaporation. On a chilly morning, you might notice droplets on grass leaves that didn't come from rain—that is condensation (dew) formed as moisture in the immediate air cooled against the grass.
components.code: Rainfall -> Puddle -> Evaporation (gas) -> Cooling aloft -> Condensation (cloud) -> Precipitation
components.code_caption: Path of a single water molecule through the cycle
components.takeaway: Every drop of water you see is participating in a cycle millions of years old.

questions.question: What primary energy source drives the entire water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy provides the heat required for evaporation and atmospheric circulation.

questions.question: What process turns water vapor into clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when rising water vapor cools and turns back into liquid droplets.

questions.question: Plants release water vapor into the air through which process?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the release of water vapor from plant leaves into the atmosphere.
